transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-06-15
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Jordan (Orion Eng Mgr), Maya (Orion ML), Samir (Orion SRE)

Summary auto-note: review of model selection, pinning, and fallbacks.

00:00 Alex (AE): okay hi everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is the weekly POC sync, should be about 45-60 minutes, agenda is quick review of your evals, then talk model pinning and rollback / fallback rules
00:18 Jordan: hey thanks Alex, yeah excited to go through the numbers, we ran the latest evals overnight, some interesting tradeoffs emerged
00:30 Priya (SE): quick housekeeping, I uploaded the benchmark spreadsheet to the shared drive, link in the chat, also note that the run includes both quantized and full fp16 variants, naming is a bit long: llama-3-70b, llama-3-70b-quant, redwood-instruct-34b, redwood-instruct-34b-legacy, and a smaller redwood-13b-quant for fallback
00:50 Maya: ok so first big takeaway is accuracy on the customer prompts — the 70b unquantized is best, obvious, but latency is painful at peak, the quantized 70b closes a lot of that gap with small drop in rouge / f1 on our extraction tasks
01:12 Samir: what's painful — we saw P95 at 820 ms for the unquantized one on our load right? and 420 ms for the quantized? those were from the short sequence tests, real-world sequences go up a bit
01:28 Priya: yep that's consistent; our runs in redwood-dedicated-like env show median around 300 for quant, p95 around 450-500 depending on batching. For the unquantized we hit p95 near 800-900 under same conditions
01:44 Jordan: cost wise how big is delta? we need per-token cost numbers to justify moving to quantized; procurement will ask
01:50 Alex: rough ballpark, quantized model variant is about 35-40% cheaper per-token in our runs due to cache and kernel savings; we'll send you updated numbers in a follow-up sheet — that's in the next steps
02:07 Maya: accuracy drop is mainly around entity extraction, sometimes hallucinations with long context — we flagged 10 failure cases that matter to the product, i'll send those
02:18 Priya: perfect, please do, that'll help calibrate regression alerts. Also, on pinning, we recommend pinning to a specific model_id + version string so you get deterministic behaviour and can control rollouts
02:33 Alex: for the pilot, we propose pinning to llama-3-70b-quant:v1.2 for normal traffic, with an automatic fallback to redwood-13b-quant:v3 if latency SLOs break or we lose capacity. That way you have a quality-first path and a cost / latency fallback
02:50 Jordan: hmm our product team is nervous about quality regressions if we fall back to 13b, will that cause user-visible churn?
02:58 Priya: yes it can; recommended approach is to only fallback at the routing layer for non-critical routes or to degrade gracefully (shorter responses, less hallucination risk) and emit a header that the client can interpret, e.g. x-redwood-model: redwood-13b-quant when fallback occurs
03:18 Samir: technical question — does the fallback happen in the same region? we need to avoid cross-region failover for latency reasons
03:25 Alex: yes, routing policies can be region-aware; we can configure fallback to prefer same-region compatible variants first, and then only cross-region as last resort
03:37 Jordan: what about rollbacks for model updates? if we pin to v1.2 then want to roll forward to v1.3 next week, what's the safest path?
03:45 Priya: canary rollout — route 5% traffic to v1.3 for 24-48 hours, monitor eval set and key metrics (p95 latency, eval F1, hallucination rate). If regression, automatic rollback to pinned version. We have a rollout DSL we can share
04:05 Maya: will the rollouts integrate with our CI so we can gate by failing tests?
04:11 Alex: yes you can push a webhook on failure to auto rollback, or we can trigger manual rollback from console. We'll send the rollout guide + example policies
04:25 Jordan: on security, we need KMS integration and audit logs for token access, is that covered for the pilot?
04:32 Alex: Yes — Redwood Private supports customer KMS/HSM, audit logs and long-term retention as an add-on. For the hosted pilot we can provide restricted log retention and SSO access. I'll share SOC2 docs and the one-pager with the exact artifacts
04:50 Samir: also need VPC peering details to pass to infra, and firewall rules for the subnets; we might do dedicated if networking is heavy
04:58 Priya: noted, Priya to include peering diagram and required ports. We also outlined earlier that dedicated pools give isolation and predictable throughput which helps p95 stability
05:12 Jordan: ok back to models — what's the recommended pinned config if we care about both quality and cost?
05:18 Priya: recommended: primary = llama-3-70b-quant:v1.2 (pinned), secondary = redwood-instruct-34b:v2.0 for higher instruction-quality tasks, fallback = redwood-13b-quant:v3 for degraded mode. Use per-route pinning so search/extract routes use the heavier model while chat uses lighter
05:38 Maya: interesting, per-route pinning should help reduce user-visible regressions, we'll need SDK hooks to select model per request, is that straightforward?
05:45 Alex: yes SDK supports per-route model config and token tagging for cost tracking; we will add the example snippet to the repo we shared
05:55 Jordan: any concerns about quantization causing new failure modes? we saw one weird truncation earlier in test 42
06:02 Priya: quant can change tokenization alignment slightly for some models; that's why we ask for failure cases. In a few cases we recommend post-processing heuristics or prompt tweaks instead of moving back to fp16
06:18 Maya: ok i'll put together the 200 prompt eval set and the top failure cases by friday
06:25 Samir: we also want a bench for steady-state throughput at 100 RPS, and a spike test at 400 for 60 seconds to see autoscale behaviour
06:33 Priya: will run both; I'll include both single-request p95 and batching throughput numbers and document autoscale triggers used in the test environment
06:45 Alex: timeline recap: Priya benches by 6/18, Alex to share pricing + security docs by 6/17, Maya gives evals by 6/20. We'll aim for a canary/rollout the week of 6/21 pending benches
06:58 Jordan: sounds good. One more thing — do we have a method to detect silent regressions after pinning? we want alerts not just raw logs
07:07 Priya: yes, Redwood Optimize can run continuous regression checks against your eval set and send alerts; we can set thresholds and integrate with your pager. We'll set up a trial alerting policy for the POC
07:22 Maya: can you include example thresholds? like 3% drop in entity F1 or 5% latency increase for p95
07:29 Alex: yes example thresholds and alert templates will be in the follow-up email.
07:36 Jordan: ok that's all from my side, thanks everyone
07:39 Alex: thanks all, we'll recap in email and list action items (see notes). End.
